newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks continued higher Friday in quiet trade, closing up 1.57 percent as Wall Street remained closed for the Independence Day holiday, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most active shares rose 209 points to 13,494 points at the close. Market turnover was 597 million reais ($557.9 million)).
"Trading volume remained fairly weak due to the holiday in the U.S.," a broker said. "The market stagnated for most of the day."
Another broker said trading volume was higher than expected on a day when Wall Street was closed and local investors were responsible for the market rise.
Blue chips posted gains across the board, with mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce preferred posting the largest gain, rising 5.91 percent to 28.49 reais.
Federal power holding Eletrobras preferred closed up 4.41 percent at 710 reais on news the company was considering a share split.
Telebras preferred closed up 1.09 percent at 175.90 reais and state oil firm Petrobras preferred moved up 1.98 percent to 309 reais.
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
